title: Bounded complexes with perfect cohomology
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $K\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that $H^i(K)=0$ outside a finite interval of integers and that, for every integer $i$, the module $H^i(K)$ in degree zero is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], that is, it admits a bounded resolution by finitely generated projective $A$-modules. Then $K$ is perfect: it is isomorphic in $D(A)$ to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules.

proof.text: Choose a cochain complex $C$ and fix an isomorphism $e:Q(C)\xrightarrow{\sim} K$ in the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $f_i:H^i(Q(C))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(C)$ for the cohomology-factorization isomorphism. Fix the identifications $\eta_i=H^i(e)\circ f_i^{-1}:H^i(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(K)$ throughout the proof. Choose integers $a\le b$ with $H^i(C)=0$ for $i<a$ or $i>b$; when all cohomology vanishes, any $a=b$ is allowed. For each integer $r$ set $K_r=Q(\tau_{\le r}C)$, using the explicit truncation in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. In degrees $i<r$ the cohomology of this truncation is $H^i(C)$: at $i=r-1$ replacing the target of $d^{r-1}$ by $\ker d^r$ does not change its kernel. At $i=r$ it is $\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}=H^r(C)$, and above $r$ its terms are zero. Thus $H^i(K_r)=H^i(K)$ for $i\le r$ and is zero for $i>r$.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical truncation of cochain complexes; setup for more-algebra Tag 066U.

proof.text: The starting object $K_{a-1}$ is perfect: Step 1 makes $\tau_{\le a-1}C$ acyclic, so the map from the zero complex to it is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and hence becomes an isomorphism in $D(A)$. The zero complex is itself a bounded finite-projective model. The same definition shows that composing a representing isomorphism with an isomorphism of derived objects preserves perfectness [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. This also proves the assertion immediately when $K$ has zero cohomology in every degree.

source.place: Tag 066U, lemma-cohomology-perfect, zero base of the finite canonical-truncation induction.

proof.text: For every $r\in[a,b]$, the hypothesis makes $H^r(K)[0]$ isomorphic to a bounded finite-projective complex $P_r$, say with bounds $u_r,v_r$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The shifted complex $P_r[-r]$ has term $P_r^{i-r}$ in degree $i$, differential $(-1)^r d_{P_r}$, and bounds $u_r+r,v_r+r$; its terms are still the same finitely generated projective modules. As $Q$ commutes with shifts [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], shifting the representing isomorphism exhibits $H^r(K)[-r]$ as a perfect object. Only these finitely many shifts are needed, so no uniform bound on all the chosen resolutions is assumed.

source.place: Tag 066U, lemma-cohomology-perfect; shift computation from the bounded finite-projective definition in Tag 0656, section-perfect.

proof.text: For each $r=a,\ldots,b$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] with the abelian category of $A$-modules, the complex $C$, and $q=r$. Its statement gives the distinguished triangle $K_{r-1}\to K_r\to H^r(C)[-r]\to K_{r-1}[1]$. Induct on $j=0,\ldots,b-a+1$ to prove that $K_{a+j-1}$ is perfect. The base $j=0$ is Step 2. If $j<b-a+1$, put $r=a+j$; the first term $K_{r-1}$ is perfect by the induction hypothesis. The isomorphism $H^r(C)\cong H^r(K)$ from Step 1 gives a chain isomorphism between the complexes with these modules in degree $r$ (its only nonzero component is this module isomorphism). Compose it with the finite-projective model from Step 3; thus the third term $H^r(C)[-r]$ is perfect. Apply [lem-sf-perfect-ring-triangle-closure] to obtain perfectness of $K_r$. This proves the induction step, including any gaps with $H^r(K)=0$.

source.place: Tag 066U, lemma-cohomology-perfect, canonical-truncation induction using Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect; triangles are derived Tag 08J5.

proof.text: At the last index Step 4 gives a bounded finite-projective model for $K_b$. The canonical inclusion $\tau_{\le b}C\to C$ induces the identity on $H^i(C)$ for $i\le b$ by the calculation in Step 1; for $i>b$ both cohomology modules vanish. It is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, so its image is an isomorphism $Q(\tau_{\le b}C)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Compose this with the fixed $e:Q(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ from Step 1 to get $K_b\cong K$, and then compose with the model of $K_b$. The resulting isomorphism with a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules is exactly perfectness of $K$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

source.place: Tag 066U, lemma-cohomology-perfect, last canonical truncation agrees with the original bounded-cohomology object.
